### 🔫 New weapon: USP-S
- A suppressed sidearm. Nobody across the map hears you shoot — the report carries about as far as a footstep instead of across the whole arena.
- It shoots noticeably straighter than every other handgun, and the price is damage: seven body shots to down a player instead of the pistol's five.
- Quiet against players only — zombies and animals never heard gunshots in the first place.

### 🛒 Shop
- The starting pistol and knife are on sale now, at the cheapest tier. Buying a Desert Eagle or a USP-S replaces your pistol, so there is finally a way to buy it back.

### 🖥️ Menu
- The main menu is rebuilt: PvE and PvP are two big cards that say what they are, with profile, settings and quit as a tidier row underneath and dev tools tucked into their own footer.
- The menu now says the game is in Early Access, shows the build number you quote in bug reports, and that it is coming to Steam.
- In the desktop build, links to the website open in your browser instead of a windowless second game window.

### 🌐 Website
- The site leads with playing in the browser, spells out what early access means here (including what is still rough), and folds the idea board into that section.

### ⚡ Performance
- Running into new terrain no longer stutters — the world streams in without the frame hitches it used to cause.
- Big hordes are far smoother: up to twice the frame rate with 80 zombies on screen.
- Zombies far from you no longer cast shadows, which is part of what pays for that.

### 🛡️ Stability
- One glitched frame can no longer freeze the game for good — it recovers and keeps playing.
- If something does stop the game, you get a message and a way back to the menu instead of a frozen screen, and a button that copies the details for a bug report.
- A graphics driver reset (or waking the machine from sleep) no longer kills the game: it says it is restoring the picture and carries on.
- One player's bad connection can no longer disrupt everyone else in the room.

### 🌲 Survival
- Trees no longer flicker out for a frame while you walk past water.
